facts.text: Middle Amana, founded by German immigrants in 1855, is the largest of the seven villages that together form a National Historic Landmark.
In 1881, Middle Amana boasted a woolen mill, starch factory, machine shop, wagon shop, blacksmith shop, book printing and bindery, brick yard, general store, school, and meeting house.
The village sits on the north side of the Iowa River valley, 1.5 miles west of Amana and 2 miles east of High Amana.
Hanh's Hearth Oven Bakery, a traditional German recipe bakery, once supplied bread and other baked goods to the communal kitchens of the Colonies.
The Amana Elementary School remains in Middle Amana, while the former Clear Creek–Amana Middle School once operated there before moving to Tiffin.
The Ruedy Kitchen House, beside the Coopershop Museum, was one of fifty kitchens that fed residents during the Colonies' communal era.
